claim: LeprPOA neurons are stimulated by warm ambient temperature and suppress energy expenditure and food intake.
source: we have previously shown that glutamatergic, long-form leptin receptor (Lepr)-expressing neurons in the POA are stimulated by warm ambient temperature and suppress energy expenditure and food intake
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Yu et al., 2016).

claim: POA Lepr signaling modulates energy expenditure in response to internal energy state.
source: We show that POA Lepr signaling modulates energy expenditure in response to internal energy state, and thus contributes to body weight homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the Lepr knockdown studies showing effects on energy expenditure during fasting and HFD feeding.

claim: POA leptin signaling is not involved in ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations.
source: However, POA leptin signaling is not involved in ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no effect of intra-POA leptin injection or Lepr knockdown on temperature-dependent changes in energy expenditure.

claim: The POA controls sympathetic nerve activity to brown adipose tissue and modulates energy expenditure to defend core body temperature in response to ambient temperature changes.
source: Notably, the POA controls sympathetic nerve activity (SNA) to brown adipose tissue (BAT) and modulates energy expenditure to defend core body temperature in response to ambient temperature changes (Morrison et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Morrison et al., 2014.

claim: Rats with POA lesions had difficulty maintaining core temperature and adjusting food intake upon ambient temperature changes.
source: For example, rats with POA lesions had difficulty not only maintaining core temperature but also adjusting food intake upon ambient temperature changes (Hamilton, 1963; Hamilton and Brobeck, 1964).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hamilton, 1963 and Hamilton and Brobeck, 1964.

claim: Chronic chemogenetic stimulation of LeprPOA neurons in mice resulted in body weight loss caused by reduced food intake that surpassed the decrease in energy expenditure.
source: Importantly, chronic chemogenetic stimulation of these neurons in mice resulted in body weight loss caused by reduced food intake that surpassed the decrease in energy expenditure.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Yu et al., 2016).

claim: Ablating Lepr in the DMH/DHA caused obesity in mice due to reduced energy expenditure without affecting food intake.
source: Another Lepr-expressing neuronal population in the dorsomedial hypothalamus/dorsal hypothalamic area (DMH/DHA) is stimulated by ambient cold and leptin, and ablating Lepr in this area caused obesity in mice due to reduced energy expenditure without affecting food intake (Zhang et al., 2011; Rezai-Zadeh et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2011 and Rezai-Zadeh et al., 2014.

claim: Leptin is required for ambient temperature-dependent food intake adjustment.
source: This possibility is further supported by studies showing that leptin is required for ambient temperature-dependent food intake adjustment (Kaiyala et al., 2015; Kaiyala et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kaiyala et al., 2015 and Kaiyala et al., 2016.

claim: 56% of LeprPOA neurons were depolarized by leptin application in the absence of synaptic transmission blockers.
source: In the absence of synaptic transmission blockers, a puff application of leptin depolarized most LeprPOA neurons (56%), while less neurons were hyperpolarized (22%) or did not change the membrane potential (22%)
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1A,C.

claim: 22% of LeprPOA neurons were hyperpolarized by leptin application in the absence of synaptic transmission blockers.
source: In the absence of synaptic transmission blockers, a puff application of leptin depolarized most LeprPOA neurons (56%), while less neurons were hyperpolarized (22%) or did not change the membrane potential (22%)
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1A,C.

claim: 22% of LeprPOA neurons showed no change in membrane potential in response to leptin application in the absence of synaptic transmission blockers.
source: In the absence of synaptic transmission blockers, a puff application of leptin depolarized most LeprPOA neurons (56%), while less neurons were hyperpolarized (22%) or did not change the membrane potential (22%)
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1A,C.

claim: Leptin treatment in the presence of synaptic transmission blockers reduced the portion of depolarized LeprPOA neurons by 20%.
source: Leptin treatment in the presence of synaptic transmission blockers (1 μM TTX +30 μM AP5 +30 μM CNQX +50 μM bicuculline) reduced the portion of depolarized neurons by 20%, indicating possible inputs from presynaptic Lepr neurons onto LeprPOA neurons
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1B,D.

claim: There are possible inputs from presynaptic Lepr neurons onto LeprPOA neurons.
source: Leptin treatment in the presence of synaptic transmission blockers (1 μM TTX +30 μM AP5 +30 μM CNQX +50 μM bicuculline) reduced the portion of depolarized neurons by 20%, indicating possible inputs from presynaptic Lepr neurons onto LeprPOA neurons
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that blocking synaptic transmission reduced leptin-induced depolarization.

claim: LeprPOA neurons represent a heterogeneous population that responds differentially to leptin.
source: These results show that LeprPOA neurons represent a heterogeneous population that responds differentially to leptin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electrophysiological data showing three different response types to leptin.

claim: Intra-POA leptin (0.05 or 0.5 pg) significantly suppressed food intake in a dose-dependent manner during the first 3 hr after injection.
source: Leptin significantly suppressed food intake in a dose-dependent manner during the first 3 hr after injection (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The leptin effect on food intake was transient and did not significantly affect total overnight food intake.
source: However, this leptin effect was transient and did not significantly affect total overnight food intake (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: The leptin effect on food intake was not due to leptin leakage to other areas, especially the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus.
source: We confirmed that this leptin effect was not due to the leptin leakage to other areas, especially the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARC), by staining for the phosphorylation of signal-transducer-and-activator-of-transcription-3 (pSTAT3), a marker for functional Lepr signaling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by pSTAT3 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Intra-POA leptin did not affect energy expenditure at any temperature condition tested (22, 30, and 10°C).
source: While acute cold and warm exposure caused expected increases and decreases in energy expenditure, respectively, intra-POA leptin did not affect energy expenditure at any temperature condition tested (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Intra-POA leptin injection had no significant effect on temperature-dependent food intake adjustment.
source: Similarly, food intake increased during 6 hr of cold exposure and decreased during 6 hr of warm exposure but intra-POA leptin injection had no significant effect on temperature-dependent food intake adjustment (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: POA leptin signaling suppresses dark-onset food intake but is not involved in acute metabolic adaptations to ambient temperature changes.
source: These data collectively indicate that POA leptin signaling suppresses dark-onset food intake but is not involved in acute metabolic adaptations to ambient temperature changes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined results from the intra-POA leptin injection experiments.

claim: AAV-GFP:Cre injection resulted in about 80% reduction of pSTAT3+ cell numbers in the POA.
source: Retrospective histological analysis of pSTAT3 revealed that we obtained about 80% Lepr KD in the POA (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pSTAT3 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Body weight and food intake did not differ between AAV-GFP and AAV-GFP:Cre groups throughout the chow diet study.
source: Throughout the study, body weight and food intake did not differ between groups (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight and food intake data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Energy expenditure did not show any group difference at any stage during the chow diet study.
source: Energy expenditure was measured once before and three times after the viral injection but did not show any group difference at any stage (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: POA Lepr is not required for body weight homeostasis or ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations under chow diet conditions.
source: Together, the results suggest that POA Lepr is not required for body weight homeostasis or ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations.
evidence: This claim is supported by the lack of phenotype in LeprPOA KD mice on chow diet.

claim: Leptin inhibits fasting-induced hypometabolism in mice.
source: However, based on leptin's well-known ability to inhibit fasting-induced hypometabolism in mice (Figure 4F)(Döring et al., 1998; Geiser et al., 1998) and weight-reduced humans (Rosenbaum and Leibel, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Leptin was unable to prevent fasting-induced hypometabolism in LeprPOA KD mice.
source: Leptin was unable to prevent fasting-induced hypometabolism in LeprPOA KD mice contrary to control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: LeprPOA KD mice failed to properly lower energy expenditure in response to fasting.
source: This was primarily due to a failure to properly lower energy expenditure in response to a negative energy state during fasting (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: There was no leptin-induced recovery of energy expenditure in LeprPOA KD mice during fasting.
source: As a result, there was no leptin-induced recovery of energy expenditure in LeprPOA KD mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by the energy expenditure data during fasting.

claim: HFD results in a positive energy balance that leads to body weight gain despite increased energy expenditure.
source: To test this possibility, we used HFD because this diet results in a positive energy balance that leads to body weight gain despite increased energy expenditure, the opposite outcome of fasting (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4F and established knowledge about HFD effects.

claim: About 50% Lepr KD was achieved in the POA in the HFD study based on pSTAT3 immunohistochemical analysis.
source: At the end of this study, we verified about 50% Lepr KD based on pSTAT3 immunohistochemical analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pSTAT3 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mice injected with AAV-GFP:Cre in the POA gained about twice as much weight as mice injected with AAV-GFP by 15 weeks after viral injection on HFD.
source: Mice injected with AAV-GFP:Cre in the POA gained about twice as much weight as mice injected with AAV-GFP by 15 weeks after viral injection (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The increase in body weight in LeprPOA KD mice on HFD was mainly due to increased fat mass.
source: This increase in body weight was mainly due to increased fat mass, as shown by a trend for increased adiposity (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by body composition data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Body weight change at week 15 showed significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers.
source: Thus, we correlated the body weight change at week 15 and the adiposity index at week 13 to POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers across all mice, and both parameters showed significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Adiposity index at week 13 showed significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers.
source: Thus, we correlated the body weight change at week 15 and the adiposity index at week 13 to POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers across all mice, and both parameters showed significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: POA Lepr signaling is important for body weight control under HFD conditions.
source: These analyses imply that POA Lepr signaling is important for body weight control under HFD conditions.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation analyses and body weight data.

claim: The increase in body fat and weight in LeprPOA KD mice was not due to increased food consumption.
source: The increase in body fat and weight was not due to increased food consumption because mice from both groups ate the same amount of food throughout the study (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: There was a trending decrease of energy expenditure in LeprPOA KD mice from week −3 to week 10 on HFD.
source: However, there was a trending decrease of energy expenditure in LeprPOA KD mice from week −3 to week 10 (Figure 5F)
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: LeprPOA KD mice showed bigger energy expenditure reduction from week −3 to week 10 compared to control mice on HFD.
source: which resulted in a bigger energy expenditure reduction from week −3 to week 10, compared to control mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by energy expenditure change data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Energy efficiency showed a weak but significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell number.
source: Energy efficiency also showed a weak but significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell number (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G), suggesting that LeprPOA KD mice spent less energy per unit food consumed.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2G.

claim: LeprPOA KD mice spent less energy per unit food consumed.
source: Energy efficiency also showed a weak but significant negative correlation with POA pSTAT3+ cell number (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G), suggesting that LeprPOA KD mice spent less energy per unit food consumed.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the energy efficiency correlation data.

claim: Expression of BAT function-related genes (Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Dio2) showed a trending decrease in LeprPOA KD mice.
source: Expression of BAT function-related genes, uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), peroxisome proliferative activated receptor gamma, coactivator one alpha (Ppargc1a, also known as Pgc1a), and deiodinase 2 (Dio2) showed a trending decrease in LeprPOA KD mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2H)
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2H.

claim: There was slightly increased but statistically non-significant increase in fat accumulation in BAT in LeprPOA KD mice.
source: Consistent with this result, there was slightly increased but statistically non-significant increase in fat accumulation in BAT in LeprPOA KD mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by BAT histology data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Systemic leptin increases thyrotropin releasing hormone (Trh) gene expression.
source: We next examined if the thyroid axis was affected in LeprPOA KD mice because systemic leptin increases thyrotropin releasing hormone (Trh) gene expression (Nillni et al., 2000; Harris et al., 2001; Guo et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nillni et al., 2000; Harris et al., 2001; Guo et al., 2004.

claim: The POA has been implicated in TRH secretion.
source: We next examined if the thyroid axis was affected in LeprPOA KD mice because systemic leptin increases thyrotropin releasing hormone (Trh) gene expression (Nillni et al., 2000; Harris et al., 2001; Guo et al., 2004) and the POA has been implicated in TRH secretion (Andersson et al., 1963; Martelli et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Andersson et al., 1963 and Martelli et al., 2014.

claim: TRH secretion leads to thyroid hormone secretion and metabolic rate increase through both central and peripheral mechanisms.
source: TRH secretion ultimately leads to thyroid hormone secretion and metabolic rate increase through both central and peripheral mechanisms (López et al., 2013; Mullur et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to López et al., 2013 and Mullur et al., 2014.

claim: Plasma levels of total triiodothyronine (T3) was only slightly and not significantly lower in LeprPOA KD mice.
source: We found that plasma levels of total triiodothyronine (T3) was only slightly and not significantly lower in LeprPOA KD mice but significantly correlated with the POA pSTAT3+ cell number (Figure 5H,I)
evidence: This claim is supported by plasma T3 data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Plasma T3 levels significantly correlated with the POA pSTAT3+ cell number.
source: We found that plasma levels of total triiodothyronine (T3) was only slightly and not significantly lower in LeprPOA KD mice but significantly correlated with the POA pSTAT3+ cell number (Figure 5H,I)
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5I.

claim: POA Lepr stimulates the thyroid axis to modulate energy expenditure.
source: suggesting that POA Lepr stimulates the thyroid axis to modulate energy expenditure.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation between plasma T3 and POA pSTAT3+ cell numbers.

claim: LeprPOA neurons project strongly to the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH) in the field of TRH neurons.
source: To corroborate this result, we observed strong projection of LeprPOA neurons to the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH) in the field of TRH neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical tracing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4A-B.

claim: A rare case of WGAGFP expression was observed in a TRH neuron in the PVH when WGAGFP was expressed in LeprPOA neurons.
source: Furthermore, when wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-GFP, an anterograde transsynaptic tracer, was expressed in LeprPOA neurons, we observed a rare case of its expression in a TRH neuron in the PVH (Figure 5—figure supplement 4C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical tracing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4C-D.

claim: Intra-POA leptin injection (0.5 pg) in fasted mice failed to significantly elevate the total T3 level.
source: However, intra-POA leptin injection (0.5 pg) in fasted mice failed to significantly elevate the total T3 level (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B), unlike the effect of systemic exogenous leptin in fasted mice on the thyroid hormone level (Ahima et al., 1996; Ahima et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by plasma T3 data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Systemic exogenous leptin in fasted mice elevates thyroid hormone levels.
source: However, intra-POA leptin injection (0.5 pg) in fasted mice failed to significantly elevate the total T3 level (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B), unlike the effect of systemic exogenous leptin in fasted mice on the thyroid hormone level (Ahima et al., 1996; Ahima et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ahima et al., 1996 and Ahima et al., 1999.

claim: Ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations in HFD-fed LeprPOA KD mice were not affected.
source: Consistent with POA Lepr KD under chow diet, ambient temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations in HFD-fed LeprPOA KD mice were not affected (data now shown).
evidence: This claim is stated but data are not shown.

claim: POA Lepr is implicated in reproductive function in female mice by promoting nitric oxide synthesis that results in luteinizing hormone (LH) release.
source: Finally, POA Lepr is implicated in reproductive function in female mice by promoting nitric oxide synthesis that results in luteinizing hormone (LH) release (Bellefontaine et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bellefontaine et al., 2014.

claim: The total number of estrous cycles during 19 days was similar between AAV-GFP and AAV-GFP:Cre groups.
source: The total number of cycles during this period was similar between groups (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by estrous cycle data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2I.

claim: POA Lepr is involved in body weight regulation by modulating energy expenditure under negative (fasting) or positive (HFD) energy balance without affecting food intake.
source: Our study demonstrates that POA Lepr is involved in body weight regulation by modulating energy expenditure under negative (fasting) or positive (HFD) energy balance without affecting food intake, which may involve the control of BAT thermogenesis and thyroid hormone release.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined results from the Lepr knockdown studies.

claim: POA Lepr involvement in body weight regulation may involve the control of BAT thermogenesis and thyroid hormone release.
source: Our study demonstrates that POA Lepr is involved in body weight regulation by modulating energy expenditure under negative (fasting) or positive (HFD) energy balance without affecting food intake, which may involve the control of BAT thermogenesis and thyroid hormone release.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed trends in BAT function and T3 levels.

claim: A direct leptin injection into the POA transiently suppresses food intake without affecting energy expenditure.
source: In contrast, a direct leptin injection into the POA transiently suppresses food intake without affecting energy expenditure.
evidence: This claim is supported by the intra-POA leptin injection experiments.

claim: The lack of leptin is generally considered a stronger signal than increasing leptin levels above normal circulating levels.
source: The lack of leptin is generally considered a stronger signal than increasing leptin levels above normal circulating levels and biological responses do not show a linear relationship with the leptin concentration (Leibel, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Leibel, 2002 and represents established knowledge.

claim: The effect of intra-POA leptin on food intake may be mediated by presynaptic Lepr expressed in neurons innervating the POA.
source: In other words, the effect on food intake may be mediated by presynaptic Lepr expressed in neurons innervating the POA, likely at axon terminals, while the effect on energy expenditure may be mediated cell autonomously in POA Lepr neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy between leptin injection and Lepr deletion effects.

claim: The effect of intra-POA leptin on energy expenditure may be mediated cell autonomously in POA Lepr neurons.
source: In other words, the effect on food intake may be mediated by presynaptic Lepr expressed in neurons innervating the POA, likely at axon terminals, while the effect on energy expenditure may be mediated cell autonomously in POA Lepr neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy between leptin injection and Lepr deletion effects.

claim: Leptin suppresses the presynaptic inhibitory AGRP neuronal input onto POMC neurons and cell autonomously stimulates POMC neurons in the ARC.
source: A similar dual mode of leptin action exists in the ARC between agouti related neuropeptide (AGRP) and pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons, in which leptin suppresses the presynaptic inhibitory AGRP neuronal input onto POMC neurons and cell autonomously stimulates POMC neurons (Cowley et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cowley et al., 2001.

claim: The POA receives inputs from many Lepr-expressing neurons including AGRP and POMC neurons.
source: The POA receives inputs from many Lepr-expressing neurons that could modulate food intake including AGRP and POMC neurons (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Leptin gene expression is inversely proportional to the SNA level to adipose tissue.
source: This reasoning was further supported by the fact that leptin gene expression is inversely proportional to the SNA level to adipose tissue (Trayhurn et al., 1995; Evans et al., 1999), which is controlled by ambient temperature and the POA.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Trayhurn et al., 1995 and Evans et al., 1999.

claim: In female Leprflox/flox mice injected with AAV-Cre in the POA, the baseline LH level was higher than that of control mice.
source: In female Leprflox/flox mice injected with AAV-Cre in the POA, the baseline LH level was higher than that of control mice and leptin failed to further induce LH secretion (Bellefontaine et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bellefontaine et al., 2014.

claim: Leptin failed to further induce LH secretion in female Leprflox/flox mice injected with AAV-Cre in the POA.
source: In female Leprflox/flox mice injected with AAV-Cre in the POA, the baseline LH level was higher than that of control mice and leptin failed to further induce LH secretion (Bellefontaine et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bellefontaine et al., 2014.

claim: Female reproduction did not seem to be affected by POA Lepr ablation based on estrous cycle measurements.
source: Despite the increased LH level in POA Lepr-ablated mice, female reproduction did not seem to be affected based on our study.
evidence: This claim is supported by the estrous cycle data showing no difference between groups.

claim: LeprPOA neurons strongly modulate BAT thermogenesis.
source: While LeprPOA neurons strongly modulate BAT thermogenesis (Yu et al., 2016), our results show no significant changes in BAT function in LeprPOA KD mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2016.

claim: Data from BAT gene expression and histology all point toward small but blunted BAT function by LeprPOA KD.
source: However, data from BAT gene expression and histology all point toward small but blunted BAT function by LeprPOA KD.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the trending but non-significant changes in BAT measurements.

claim: The AAV-GFP:Cre injection into the POA achieved only about 50% Lepr KD on average in the HFD study.
source: Lastly, it is important to point out that our AAV-GFP:Cre injection into the POA achieved only about 50% Lepr KD on average in the HFD study.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pSTAT3 analysis.

claim: Partial ablation of POA Lepr and inherent variability of viral injections contributed to relatively small effect sizes and big standard errors.
source: We believe this partial ablation of POA Lepr and inherent variability of viral injections contributed to relatively small effect sizes and big standard errors that rendered many measurement differences between groups statistically insignificant.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the experimental approach.

claim: The contribution of POA leptin signaling to energy balance and body weight homeostasis may be underestimated in this study.
source: Therefore, the contribution of POA leptin signaling to energy balance and body weight homeostasis may be underestimated in our study.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential underestimation of effects due to incomplete knockdown.

claim: This study is the first to link POA leptin signaling to body weight control.
source: Our study is the first to link POA leptin signaling to body weight control.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: HFD promotes a higher metabolic rate.
source: HFD promotes a higher metabolic rate and POA Lepr may be necessary for this HFD-induced increase in energy expenditure.
evidence: This claim is supported by the energy expenditure data showing increased metabolic rate with HFD.

claim: POA Lepr may be necessary for the HFD-induced increase in energy expenditure.
source: HFD promotes a higher metabolic rate and POA Lepr may be necessary for this HFD-induced increase in energy expenditure.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that LeprPOA KD mice showed blunted energy expenditure increase on HFD.

claim: The loss of POA Lepr may have accelerated the body weight gain caused by HFD in LeprPOA KD mice.
source: Therefore, the loss of POA Lepr may have accelerated the body weight gain caused by HFD in LeprPOA KD mice.
evidence: This is an inference from the body weight and energy expenditure data.

claim: The study proposes a potential integration of environmental temperature information and internal energy state in the POA through neural and humoral routes, respectively.
source: Our study also proposes a potential integration of environmental temperature information and internal energy state in the POA through neural and humoral routes, respectively.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the overall findings.

claim: Acute temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations did not interact with POA leptin signaling.
source: Even though acute temperature-dependent metabolic adaptations did not interact with POA leptin signaling, the long-term interaction still remains to be investigated.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing no interaction.
